clue.text: Boundary in dispute after cautious declaration

indicators.note: after places the word for dispute behind the cautious declaration in the answer

parts.note: a hedge is a non-committal statement that guards against being wrong
a row is a quarrel or argument

explanation.surface: Two neighbours start a border quarrel right after one of them makes a carefully guarded statement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boundary in dispute' reads as one phrase, but 'Boundary' alone is the definition and 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A line of shrubs planted along a field edge marks the limit of a property, so it is a type of boundary.

clue.text: Give sustenance to killer periodically behind copper's back

indicators.note: behind puts the picked letters after the copper piece
back tells us to read the copper's letters in the opposite direction

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper, plus the S of the possessive

indicators.note: periodically means taking letters at regular intervals, here the first, third and fifth

explanation.surface: A murderer is somehow fed while standing behind a policeman's back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns CU'S into SUC; 'periodically' takes K, L, E from 'killer'.
explanation.definitionFit: To feed a baby or young animal at the breast or teat is to nourish it, giving it sustenance.

clue.text: Note: building block doesn't finish framework

parts.note: fa is a note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: doesn't finish means the last letter of the building block is lost

parts.note: a brick is the basic block a wall is built from

explanation.surface: A memo complaining that a building block was never completed, so the framework is unfinished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note:' looks like a heading for a memo, but it supplies FA.
explanation.definitionFit: The underlying structure of a building or of society is its basic framework, the sense in 'the fabric of the church'.

clue.text: Crown and orb out of alignment

parts.note: an orb is a sphere, a round object
something misaligned is off, not quite right

explanation.surface: The royal crown and orb have been set down crookedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crown' and 'orb' suggest regalia, but 'Crown' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To crown something is to complete it with a finishing touch, which is what this phrasal verb means.

clue.text: Headgear from The King and I placed on record

indicators.note: placed on puts the king and I around the record, one on either side

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A costume hat from the musical The King and I, put on display on an album.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The King and I' looks like the musical's title, but it splits into K and I either side of EP.
explanation.definitionFit: A kepi is a French military cap with a flat circular top and a peak, so it is a type of headgear.

clue.text: Lifting articles kept apart by travelling pilgrims

indicators.note: the pilgrims on the move get mixed up, and the two articles end up separated among their letters

parts.note: a is the indefinite article, and two of them are needed

explanation.surface: Pilgrims on the road keep their belongings separated so nothing is stolen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling' rearranges PILGRIMS, and 'kept apart by' sets the two A's in separate places among those letters: PL-A-GI-A-RISM.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifting is slang for stealing, and copying someone else's writing as one's own is literary theft.

clue.text: Traditional play script retaining a touch of high spirits

indicators.note: retaining means the play and script hold the next letter within them

parts.note: panto is short for pantomime, the traditional British Christmas stage show

indicators.note: a touch of means just the first letter of the word that follows

parts.note: MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a handwritten script

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned play's script keeps a hint of high spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high spirits' looks like one phrase; 'high' gives H and 'spirits' alone is the definition. A panto is a British family Christmas show with slapstick and audience participation.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghosts and apparitions are spirits of the dead, and both words name the same ghostly figures.

clue.text: Against wearing any exotic shade

indicators.note: wearing means the rearranged letters are worn around the next piece, enclosing it
exotic suggests something strange, so the letters of any are rearranged

parts.note: v is short for versus, meaning against

explanation.surface: Someone opposed to wearing any unusual colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exotic' turns ANY into NAY; 'wearing' puts it round V.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark blue colour named after naval uniforms is a shade, just as crimson or teal are.

clue.text: Drawn-out attempts at wit last to start

indicators.note: last to start means the final letter moves to the front

parts.note: puns are plays on words, attempts at wit

explanation.surface: Tedious attempts at humour, with the last one only now getting going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last to start' moves the final S of PUNS to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A story that has been stretched out at length is drawn out, as in 'a long-winded tale'.

clue.text: Knights are at odds, holding line to rear of Greek cross

indicators.note: to rear of puts the at-odds piece behind the Greek letter

parts.note: chi is the Greek letter shaped like a cross, X

indicators.note: holding means the word for at odds contains the next letter

parts.note: to vary is to differ, to be at odds

explanation.surface: Knights disagree, keeping a line behind a cross-shaped formation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts L inside the word for at odds; 'to rear of' places that after the Greek letter, which is shaped like a cross.
explanation.definitionFit: The collective body of mounted knights, or the knightly code, is the old sense of this word for medieval cavalry.

clue.text: Stuff from returning craft brought in by criminal gang?

indicators.note: brought in by means the reversed craft is placed inside the criminal gang

parts.note: a con is a convict, a criminal
a band is a group or gang

indicators.note: returning means the word for craft goes backwards

parts.note: art is skill or craft

explanation.surface: Goods smuggled in by a crooked gang off a boat coming home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' reverses the word for craft, and 'brought in by' sets it inside the criminal gang. 'craft' suggests a boat but means skill.
explanation.definitionFit: Smuggled goods are stuff in the loose sense of material or articles, prohibited ones here.

clue.text: Fishy lot providing police evidence?

definitions.meaning: a number of small flatfish of the flounder family

explanation.surface: Something suspicious handed over as proof to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: Dab is a small flatfish, so several are a fishy lot, and British police slang calls fingerprints by the same word.

clue.text: River maiden, charmer without aspiration

parts.note: a miss is an unmarried girl, a maiden

indicators.note: aspiration is the sound of H, so without aspiration means dropping the letter H

parts.note: a houri is a beautiful nymph of Islamic paradise, a charmer

explanation.surface: A list of a river, a young woman and a seductress lacking ambition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aspiration' looks like ambition, but in phonetics it is the breathy H sound, removed from HOURI.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a long North American waterway, a major tributary of the Mississippi.

clue.text: Trenchant section of the law one's taken into account

indicators.note: taken into means the police section and one go inside the account

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the detective branch of British police
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A cutting legal clause that someone has factored in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the law' means the police here, not legislation; the CID is the plain-clothes detective branch of British police.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharp, biting remarks can be called sour or caustic, so a trenchant comment is cutting in the same way.

clue.text: Model's ignored at church

indicators.note: ignored means the word at is left out

parts.note: a template is a pattern or model to copy

explanation.surface: A fashion model has been snubbed at church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model's ignored at' reads as 'model is ignored at church'; in fact 'at' is the word ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: A building for worship is often called by this name, and some churches and synagogues use it.

clue.text: Limited edition, limited edition

parts.note: a number is one issue or edition of a magazine
ed is the abbreviation for edition, the word cut short

explanation.surface: A phrase repeated, as if printed on two copies of a short print run.
explanation.walkthrough: The repetition looks like a double definition, but it is definition plus charade: NUMBER for an issue, and ED, an edition limited to two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: When your days are counted they are restricted in quantity, so finite things are said to be counted off like this.

clue.text: Get rid of Times by end of decade

indicators.note: by places the last letter beside the times

parts.note: eras are long periods of time

indicators.note: end of means the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Scrap the Times newspaper before the decade is out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper but is a plain plural.
explanation.definitionFit: To wipe out writing or a recording is to remove it completely, to get rid of it.

clue.text: Donor taking to pieces intricate construction

indicators.note: taking something to pieces breaks it up, so these letters are reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: A donor dismantles an elaborate structure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' belongs to the anagram fodder, not the indicator; only 'to pieces' signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Legend says Alexander cut a fiendishly tangled knot at Gordium, so the phrase names any intricate tangle or construction.

clue.text: Police's case held up by priest that gathers info

indicators.note: held means the reversed casing is enclosed by the priest

parts.note: a rector is a parish priest

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the letters read upwards, in reverse
case means the outer letters, the casing of the word

explanation.surface: A priest picks up the police's case file to gather intelligence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' takes the outside letters of 'Police'; 'up' reverses them, as this is a down clue; 'held' puts that pair inside the priest.
explanation.definitionFit: A sense organ or nerve ending that detects stimuli collects information for the body.

clue.text: Analyst's technique showing promise with club

parts.note: to give your word is to promise
an association is a club or society

explanation.surface: A psychoanalyst's method shows potential when combined with a club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Analyst' is a psychoanalyst here, who asks patients for the first thing a prompt brings to mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Psychoanalysts use the method of free response to prompt words to reveal unconscious links in a patient's mind.

clue.text: Workplace gives away boxes I'd knocked up

indicators.note: knocked up in a down clue means turned upwards, so the letters read in reverse
boxes means the word for gives away encloses the next piece

parts.note: to out someone is to expose or give them away
taken as written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: An office worker says the workplace is giving away boxes they hastily built.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxes' puts I'D inside the word for gives away; 'knocked up' reads the result upwards. 'knocked up' looks like an anagram cue, but in a down clue 'up' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's or photographer's workroom, or a broadcasting room, is a place of work.

clue.text: Fish bones brought up

indicators.note: brought up in a down clue means read from bottom to top, in reverse

parts.note: Bones, short for sawbones, is slang for a doctor, abbreviated doc

explanation.surface: A fish with its bones brought back up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bones' looks like fish bones but is slang for a doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a common North Atlantic food fish, the one in British fish and chips.

clue.text: Eg Mae West rival's fee outrageous

indicators.note: outrageous means wild and shocking, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: An actress's rival demands a scandalous fee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mae West' looks like the actress, but airmen named their inflatable life jacket after her bust.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mae West was RAF slang for an inflatable life jacket, an example of rescue equipment that keeps a person afloat.

clue.text: Commoners highly offensive, also smooth

parts.note: rank means foul-smelling, highly offensive
and means also, in addition
to file is to smooth with a rasp

explanation.surface: Ordinary people are rather rude yet suave.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinary members of a group, without rank or title, as opposed to its leaders, are its common people.

clue.text: Large plug with switching is not stopping entrance

indicators.note: stopping means the rearranged letters plug a gap inside the big promotion

parts.note: hype is big publicity, a large plug for a product

indicators.note: switching means the letters swap places into a new order

explanation.surface: A big stopper with a switch fails to block a doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switching' rearranges IS NOT; 'stopping' sets those letters inside the big plug. 'entrance' is a verb, not a doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrance, stressed on the second syllable, is to put into a trance, to bewitch.

clue.text: On exchange of capital, succeed in getting thermal energy source

indicators.note: capital means initial letter, so the first letters of the two words trade places

parts.note: to find something is to succeed in getting it
thermal means warm

explanation.surface: A financial deal that succeeds in getting a heat-energy source.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks financial but means first letter: FIND and WARM swap initials.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of wind turbines generating electricity is a source of renewable energy.

clue.text: Formal greeting recalled as something requiring pluck

indicators.note: recalled means the word as is called back, read in reverse

parts.note: a lute is a stringed instrument that is plucked

explanation.surface: A formal greeting remembered as something that takes courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pluck' seems to mean courage but means plucking strings.
explanation.definitionFit: A military gesture of respect, such as raising the hand to the brow, is a formal greeting.

clue.text: Flat green playing area sound for horses

indicators.note: sound says the word is heard aloud rather than spelt

parts.note: bays are reddish-brown horses

explanation.surface: A level green pitch that is fine for horses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like 'healthy' but signals a homophone. The green cloth covers snooker and billiard tables.
explanation.definitionFit: The green felt covering a snooker or card table is the flat surface the game is played on.

clue.text: Singer's concession

definitions.meaning: short for soprano's, the voice part or the singer taking it, as in a choral score
something given to appease or placate, a small sweetener

explanation.surface: A vocalist has made a grudging allowance.
explanation.walkthrough: Choral scores abbreviate the soprano part, so 'Singer's' stands for that abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: the abbreviation for a soprano voice, and a placating gift offered to keep someone quiet.
